name: competitive-gap-analysis
description: Somebody sends you a link to a tool and asks "can we do this?" — this answers it properly. Reads what the tool ACTUALLY does (transcribes the video, fetches the page; never trusts the caption), breaks it into discrete capabilities, checks each one against what your system already has, and ends with a verdict — already have it, build the gap, adopt it, or ignore — with the reasoning written down. Evaluates repositories read-only, never by running them.

steps.title: Get what the thing actually does
Break it into capabilities you can check one at a time
Check every capability against what you already have
Repositories are read, never run
One of four, in writing, with the reasoning
Record it so the next person does not redo it

name: freelabel-ads
description: Take an ad from an idea to a published post — brief, branded creative, caption, a human approval gate, then publish to the brand's own connected accounts. Stops at the gate by default; publishing is a separate, deliberate act. Creative comes from the existing campaign-image tools, publishing from the ownership-enforced social layer.

steps.title: Which accounts can this brand actually run ads from
Turn the topic into an ad brief
Render the branded graphic and host it
Write the post caption
Approve before anything goes public
Publish the ad

name: pathways-intake-review
description: Take an intake case from "documents collected" to "assigned to a navigator" — evidence checked on the machine that holds the records, risk and workload computed, and a physician approving both the case and the assignment on one screen.

steps.title: Check the case file is complete
Summarise the records and set a risk tier
Suggest a navigator, with reasoning
Physician approves the case AND the assignment

name: bills-to-books
description: Turn a folder of bills, receipts and invoices into verified ledger entries you can hand an accountant. Reads each document, converts foreign currency at the rate for that day, refuses to write any figure it cannot find on the document, and ends with a reconciliation that ties every reported number back to the rows behind it. Preview by default — nothing is written until you say so.

steps.title: Look at what you actually have before spending anything
Read the folder — preview, nothing written
Read the HELD pile. This is the step people skip
Commit, once you have read the held pile
Prove the numbers tie out
What to give the accountant

name: daily-brief
description: Produce The Daily Brief — collect the music-industry wire, feed the FREELABEL newsroom, get an article approved in the dashboard, then render the 9-page brief. Nine pages, six figure shapes, and a renderer that refuses to draw a claim it cannot source. Pass a date or "today" (e.g. "today", "2026-08-20", "audit only").

name: atlas-epic
description: Start a piece of work the way it should be started — an epic written BEFORE the work, published so the user can watch it without asking for status, existing bugs attached instead of duplicated, and a diary entry at the end that records what you got wrong. Work that isn't written down gets re-derived; a user who can't see what you're doing can't redirect you.

steps.title: Find what already exists
Draft the epic before the work, not after
Publish it and hand over the URL
Confirm the write actually landed
Wire the work into the graph — three seams, then govern it
Decide whether to fan out — and to WHAT, before deciding how many
Hand it to the loop — only when the work is loop-shaped
Do the work, and keep the epic current
Write the diary

name: desktop-release
description: Ship the IRIS desktop app (desktop-v1.18.x, from iris/1.18.23) without shipping the wrong thing. Preview a change from a compiled build, gate it locally because CI's test runners do not run, preflight against a concurrent release, dispatch, diagnose a failed platform build from its job log, and confirm the version at the endpoint the in-app updater reads.

name: genesis-artifact
description: Ship a branded bespoke Genesis /p/ artifact — a hand-designed HTML page that takes its colour and type from the brand's own design tokens rather than from taste, shows real captures rather than mockups, and is verified in a browser by reading the DOM rather than by trusting a screenshot.

steps.title: Pull the brand's tokens before choosing a single colour
Read the standard, then answer check 01 out loud
Capture, crop and host any page the artifact shows
Write the fragment — scoped, tokenised, host-themed
Build the JSON by script and batch-publish it
Verify by reading the DOM, never by looking at a picture
Score it, and record what you got wrong

name: agentic-loop
description: Stop babysitting a long multi-step task by hand. Point this at a goal and it plans the work, fans it out to specialists, checks its own output against what you actually asked for, and remembers what it learned for next time — optionally repeating itself on a weekly schedule with nobody there to kick it off. The same engine behind the Builder, Scout, and Growth demos, generalized to any goal you give it.

steps.title: Prove the services exist BEFORE spending a cycle on them
Orchestrator — discover & plan
Builder — one-shot the artifact
Scout — ranked opportunities
Growth — 48-hour activation + self-check
Verification — did we hit the goal?
Orchestrator — unified plan + next-steps
Is the loop finished? Run the check; do not ask the model
Persist memory (+ ingest to bloq)
Wire the weekly cadence
Cycle summary

name: payable-benchmark
description: Score pathways:provider-payable against one of Robyn's filed Case Provider Reports and record the run, so "are we getting better" is a number with a history instead of an opinion. Two metrics scored apart — COVERAGE moves when a data source lands, FIDELITY moves when the maths reads the right field — and a hard rule that zero parsed rows exits red and never scores. Built 2026-09-12 after an ad-hoc scorer printed "the field is empty book-wide" from a list that was empty because the query had timed out.

steps.title: The inputs exist and the interpreter is there
Score it, and refuse to score nothing
What has moved, and whether the label says why
